Convert a study's definition sheets to the YAML spec

Source: R/convert.R
tfl_convert_sheets_to_yaml.Rd

Reads the definition files of a study folder as tflplanner wrote them – study.yml, spec/table_spec.xlsx, spec/report_spec.xlsx, spec/ard_definition.json (or spec/ard_spec.xlsx), spec/listing_figure_spec.xlsx, spec/figures/<id>.yml – and writes the YAML spec to to: study.yml, spec/data.yml, spec/defaults.yml, spec/codelists.yml, spec/patterns/<name>.yml, spec/toc.yml and one spec/outputs/<id>.yml a report. Loose files (a table and a report workbook alone) convert too: from may be a folder holding them.

Usage

tfl_convert_sheets_to_yaml(
  from,
  to,
  content_fn = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  figures = c("design", "items")
)

tfl_yaml_from_sheets(
  sheets,
  to,
  content_fn = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  figures = c("design", "items")
)

Arguments

from

The study folder (or a folder of the definition files).

to

The folder to write to (made if missing; spec/ under it).

content_fn

A function (spec, output_id) returning a list of tfl_item() for a table (output_id = NA for the defaults). NULL: the package's own bridge from the sheets to the layers (.plan_content_from_sheets()) when it is there, else none.

overwrite

Write over files already in to?

figures

How a figure is written: "design" (default) its designer's pieces as the content's items, as the figure designer reads them; "items" its content of function calls, plot by plot (tfl_fig_content_from_design(): ggplot, geom_line, ..., tfl_image), the form the designer is moving to.

sheets

The definition as objects, a list: table (a tfl_table_spec, or its sheets; the report sheets with them), planner (tflplanner's _tflplanner sheet: the report list and the setup code), ard (the ARD sheets), listing (listings, listing_cols), figures (a figure's design list, by id), study (study.yml's fields). What the app holds, or what the workbooks read as.

Value

Invisibly, a list: to, files (paths written), not_converted (a data frame: output, sheet, row, column, reason, value).

Details

A table's content: (its layers) is made by content_fn(spec, output_id) – the bridge from the sheets to the plan's layers; without one, the content is left empty and said so in _not_converted.yml. Cells that hold R (where, derive, args, post, code, when) are kept as !r text and listed; (none) becomes !unset.

Use, in R:“`r r <- tfl_convert_sheets_to_yaml("C:/studies/ABC-101", "C:/studies/ABC-101-yaml") r$files # what was written r$not_converted # what was not, or changed form (also _not_converted.yml) tfl_read_outputs(r$to) # the reports, read back
